claim: For every complex \(4\times4\) matrix \(A\) with constant positive middle Hermitian-pencil gap \(d=\lambda_2-\lambda_3>0\) in every direction, the two middle eigenvalues are first angular harmonics centered at a unique \(c\); the rank-two numerical range \(\Lambda_2(A)\) is a disk of radius \(d/2\), and the characteristic determinant pencil contains the corresponding circular quadratic factor.
integrity: The proof is exact and self-contained apart from the standard Li–Sze half-plane identity, with a proved specialized-gcd root-location lemma; no finite numerical test is used as an infinite certificate.
limitations: Hypothesis concerns direction-independent raw middle eigenvalue gap, not the geometric width of rank-two numerical range.
No converse, zero-gap or higher-dimensional rigidity claim.
Older implicit reformulations remain a literature risk.
title: Four-dimensional middle-gap rigidity for rank-two numerical ranges
